name: MaterialIQ Step-10 ground truth

label_vocabulary.MATCH: Both records describe the SAME physical item: category, type and every critical technical attribute agree (series/seal/bore for bearings; pressure class/size/type for valves; voltage/power/phase for motors; suction/discharge for pumps; thread/diameter/length/grade for fasteners). Manufacturer may differ only where the records are otherwise fully specified and cross-brand equivalence is still an engineering judgement — such pairs are labelled NEEDS_REVIEW, not MATCH.
label_vocabulary.NEEDS_REVIEW: The records plausibly describe the same or interchangeable item, but a human must decide: a critical specification conflicts (2RS vs ZZ, Class 150 vs 300, 415V vs 230V), a critical attribute is present on only one side, the item is a kit/assembly variant, or the pair is cross-brand.
label_vocabulary.NOT_A_MATCH: The records describe clearly different items: different categories, different types (nut vs stud, gate vs check, submersible vs centrifugal), or conflicting critical dimensions/series that no procurement context would conflate.

protocol: Labels derive from the technical attributes stored on each record (visible in Material Master), NOT from engine output. Every pair is cross-CPSE. expect_conflict marks pairs where the engine's evidence SHOULD name the given attribute (critical|missing); pairs without it test ambiguity handling instead.
